highlights.title: Vivo’s X Fold 6 accidentally feels like a throwback
highlights.summary: It's a quirk of the release calendar that when Vivo's X Fold 6 launched in China this June, it was just another foldable. Now that it's ready for its global release, the size and aspect ratio feel oddly old-fashioned.
body: The tall, square-ish foldable is now launching internationally, after releasing in China this summer.

The X Fold 6 is much the same size as Vivo’s previous foldables, and most other foldables that launched before both Apple and Samsung pivoted to a shorter, wider form factor with the Z Fold 8 and iPhone Duo. The 6.51-inch cover display is in the standard smartphone 20:9 aspect ratio, opening to an almost square 8.02-inch panel. The crease is a little behind rivals, since it’s quite visible, and the IP59 rating is good but not great.

Where the X Fold 6 stands out is its cameras. The 1/1.4-inch-type, 200-megapixel main camera sensor is one of the biggest on any foldable phone (only Huawei uses bigger), and it’s paired with 50-megapixel telephoto and ultrawide cameras that also look decent. The 6,900mAh battery isn’t bad either, with a custom “Super Edition” of the MediaTek Dimensity 9500 running the show.

highlights.title: Price books Clayton showdown at World Grand Prix as Aspinall races through
highlights.summary: Gerwyn Price set up an all-Welsh quarter-final showdown with Jonny Clayton with a straight-sets win over Ross Smith at the World Grand Prix, as Ryan Joyce and Nathan Aspinall also progressed in Leicester.
body: Price, among the tournament favourites after Luke Littler's shock early exit, followed his opening-round victory over Sebastian Białecki by dropping just four legs to despatch Smith at the Mattioli Arena.

The 2020 champion was outscored by Smith - having posted the highest average of the first round - but dropped just four legs during his 3-0 win, securing him a meeting with World Cup of Darts partner Clayton on Friday evening.

Clayton opened with three consecutive ton-plus checkouts and made four in total during a 3-1 victory over Wessel Nijman, where a 93.08 average and some remarkable finishing pushed him past the 12th seed.

Ryan Joyce breezed into the quarter-finals with a straight-sets victory over Danny Noppert, as Luke Woodhouse - who stunned Littler in the first round - was knocked out after losing 3-0 to Nathan Aspinall in a one-sided contest.

highlights.title: Google announces Gemini 4 and says it’s so capable that only ‘trusted cyber defenders’ can have it right now
highlights.summary: Google today revealed its next AI frontier model, which it's calling Gemini 4 Argon. The new model delivers "frontier performance in complex workflows across real-world software engineering, enterprise knowledge work like legal and finance, and cybersecurity defense," according to chief AI…
body: Gemini 4 Argon is launching first in a limited capacity so Google can make sure it’s not misaligned.

Kavukcuoglu says Gemini 4 Argon is already powering Google’s “internal workflows,” highlighting how the model has helped with tasks like large-scale codebase migrations. Google also shared a big chart showing many benchmarks where Gemini 4 fares better than competing models from OpenAI and Anthropic. (The AI community was buzzing earlier this week on X over what appeared to be leaked benchmarks for the new model.) Google will be strengthening “critical frontier safeguards” before a broader rollout, including defending against misuse and prompt injection attacks and monitoring for misalignment.

The launch of Gemini 4 Argon comes just a day after OpenAI’s splashy DevDay conference, where OpenAI launched its Dots AI agent and GPT-6.1 Sol AI model. (OpenAI also said this week that it wouldn’t be releasing a planned GPT-6.1 Astra model due to worries about safety.) It’s also arriving soon after Kavukcuoglu’s appointment as the new boss of DeepMind in August.

highlights.title: 6 Switch 2 Games Releasing in October 2026 You Officially Cannot Miss
highlights.summary: It's October, which means we're in the thick of the fall and gaming's busiest release season. In most years, October serves as the annual climax of the release schedule — but not this year.
body: Nevertheless, October will be plenty busy enough for Switch 2 owners. The deluge of ports continues, along with some tasty Switch 2 upgrades for existing Switch games, including the two Octopath Traveler games and Minecraft. Nintendo has its traditional monthly exclusive in the form of a massive casual/family gaming comeback; Square Enix brings another retro RPG to the system; and a huge AAA multiplatform arrives on Nintendo, on day one, for the first time in a very long time. Here are our top six picks for the month.

October's most notable game is this indie puzzle game, developed by Jonathan Blow, the creator of Braid and The Witness. Blow is a prickly, problematic person, and there are some questions about authorship and credit with Order of the Sinking Star, which is based on several other sokoban (block-pushing) puzzle games. But Blow's genius as a designer of puzzles is undeniable, and this game is set up as a nearly bottomless well of fiendlishly clever head-scratchers.

highlights.title: Europe's CPC targets King, Supercell, Mojang and others over virtual currencies
highlights.summary: Europe's Consumer Protection Cooperation Network is taking "coordinated actions" against a string of top games companies as it looks to investigate compliance with 'Key Principles' on in-game virtual currencies announced last year.
body: The CPC is a network of national authorities responsible for the enforcement of EU consumer protection laws. It has asked Activision Blizzard, Crytek, InnoGames, King, Mojang, Plarium, PLR Worldwide Sales, Riot Games, Supercell and Ubisoft to bring their commercial practices in line relating to in-game virtual currencies.

Games being assessed include Hunt: Showdown 1896, Forge of Empires, Candy Crush Saga, Minecraft, Mech Arena, Gardenscapes, Valorant, Clash of Clans, For Honor, Diablo Immortal and Call of Duty Mobile.

The games were selected for assessment by the CPC Network "in the context of a wide-scale market compliance check due to broad reach, cross-device accessibility, and varied age ratings, all of which amplify the impact of the practices on consumers".
It's not clear what, if any, 'Key Principles' have not been adhered to prior to the CPC Network opening its investigations.

highlights.title: How AI could ‘supercharge’ election risks across south-east Asia
highlights.summary: Some experts fear AI could be weaponised in south-east Asia, home to nations with predominately young and hyper-connected populations. Years ago it would have been an elaborate operation involving any army of cyber troops creating fake news websites, social media accounts and forged dossiers, all…
body: In a worrying sign of how AI could “supercharge” fake news, Anthropic recently revealed how Claude AI was used in a political influence operation in Malaysia. It created a commercial election manipulation platform, utilising a network of about 1,000 X accounts, a fake news outlet called “Malaysia Pulse” and a series of fabricated documents.

The operation appeared designed to target voters in in recent state elections, pulling in census and electoral data to exploit sensitive political and social fractures, including race, religion, and royalty across all 222 Malaysian parliamentary constituencies.

The experiment was ultimately ineffective once Anthropic stepped in but has sparked alarm about how AI could be weaponised in future elections in south-east Asia, a region already deeply vulnerable to fake news.
Katie Harbath, who formerly worked on public policy for global elections at Meta, says the case is an example of how AI brings a new level of sophistication and ease to the disinformation landscape.

highlights.title: The Battle to Be Your Personal AI Agent Is Here
highlights.summary: OpenAI's Dots and Meta's Muse are vying to be your AI agent of choice. I've tried both—and I suspect you will too.
body: Yesterday, I spent the morning at OpenAI ’s annual DevDay, where over 2,500 nerds discussed building software and marveled at the latest artificial intelligence models. The biggest reveal of the day was Dots, the company’s new, always-on agents that proactively help complete tasks and make autonomous decisions as they scour the web.

After watching the sometimes messy demos on stage and hearing CEO Sam Altman talk about his experiences using the agents, I was curious what it felt like to boss my own Dot around. I’ve spent most of September testing another cute, cuddly agent, Meta’s Muse, and I wanted to know how OpenAI’s user experience would compare.

I named mine “Toolie” and tweaked it to look like a pink frog. As midnight approached and my partner slept soundly nearby, I started whispering sweet nothings to Toolie. I called my personalized bot through ChatGPT, asking what tasks it was best at. “My strongest work is taking a messy, time-consuming task and turning it into something you can use,” it responded. OK, sure. Let’s get to work.
points: OpenAI's Dots and Meta's Muse are vying to be your AI agent of choice.

highlights.title: Lego's Sony PlayStation Set Officially Launches This Week
highlights.summary: After bringing the Nintendo Entertainment System, Atari 2600, and Sega Genesis to life in brick form, Lego is teaming up with PlayStation for a new retro console recreation. The Lego PlayStation set is finally here and launches Oct. 1.
body: The Lego Sony PlayStation is a 1,911-piece set that is designed to "near 1:1 scale" and will cost $179.99. The set lets players build the original PlayStation console and controller in Lego brick form, as well as some dioramas that nod to PlayStation's early history. The Lego PlayStation set features a functioning "Open" button on the front-right corner of the build, which opens the system's spring-loaded lid to reveal a pair of nostalgic dioramas. Inside the Lego PlayStation is a large Lego recreation of the classic "PS" logo, as well as mini dioramas based on 1997's Gran Turismo and 1999's Ape Escape.

At 1,911 pieces, the Lego Sony PlayStation is smaller than the Lego Atari 2600 (2,532 pieces) and Lego Nintendo Entertainment System (2,646 pieces), but larger than the Lego Sega Genesis (480 pieces). All of Lego's video game console sets have had varied extras, including a retro TV set for the Lego NES and multiple cartridges for the Lego 2600.
Lego's PlayStation set will officially be released on Oct. 1 for Lego Insiders and Oct. 4 for everyone. It will be available from Lego.com.

highlights.title: For One Night, Lauren Halsey and Erykah Badu Turned the Hollywood Bowl Into a Funk Fantasia
highlights.summary: “Usually, the cadence for an art project is you get the work, you complete the work, you get the work to the gallery, and that’s the work,” Halsey explains to Vogue. This, however, was “a whole ecosystem.”
body: On Monday afternoon, less than 24 hours before the debut of what was inarguably Lauren Halsey’s biggest artistic presentation to date, things were a little frenzied in her South Los Angeles workshop. When she signed on for our Zoom interview, members of her team could be seen weaving in and out of the frame behind her, carrying everything from a neon-painted pharaoh to a plastic light-up palm tree.

“There’s this level in funk where you’re ‘on the one,’” said the lifelong funkateer, a devotee of George Clinton’s Parliament-Funkadelic and its psychedelic, Afrofuturist universe. “You’ve reached your highest level of your interplanetary function, and that means everything is in the perfect flow. I feel like that even though I’m so stressed.”

The following evening, the artist, known for building maximalist architectural environments that sample and remix the signs, storefronts, symbols, people, and visual language of South Central LA, would attempt something the Hollywood Bowl had never seen before: a fine artist transforming the storied amphitheater and its grounds and staff uniforms into a world of her own making.

highlights.title: Elon Musk’s Grokipedia has a ‘newly refreshed’ design
highlights.summary: Grokipedia, SpaceXAI's AI-powered competitor to Wikipedia, recently started incorporating edits again, and today, it got some design tweaks as part of a v0.3 update, including a new logo and refreshes to its homepage and live edits page.
body: The AI-powered Grokipedia, which recently started updating again after months without edits, just got some visual updates.

Grokipedia’s old homepage was pretty much just a logo and a search bar, but the updated homepage includes a list of featured articles, a list of the most-read articles, and a tracker showing the “latest edits.” The new featured list showcases digital representations of books that you can spin around, and the most read section also uses the book metaphor with a horizontally-scrolling shelf of “book” spines. On the new live edits page, it’s easier to see more of the recent changes at once.

Article pages have a few new design tweaks, too, including a nicer-looking format for the tables at the top of articles with key facts and smaller spacing between lines of text. Otherwise, at least from what I can tell, articles themselves look largely the same.

highlights.title: There Are Plenty of Reasons to Be Concerned About Bioweapons Development—Even Without AI
highlights.summary: In her new book on biological warfare, Annie Jacobsen didn’t even discuss AI because scientists can already warp Mother Nature to create extinction-level events.
body: This story originally appeared on Mother Jones and is part of the Climate Desk collaboration.

We’ve been hearing a great deal recently about the specter of AI-driven human extinction. Maybe our misplaced trust in AI intelligence will set off World War III. Or AI agents will unleash widespread cyberattacks and take over the internet. Given too much autonomy, the machines will run amok. They may seek to deceive their creators—wait, that’s already happened. Suppose they conclude, like Agent Smith in The Matrix, that “human beings … are a plague, and we are the cure.” Or perhaps the chatbots help bad humans unleash a literal plague—a biological weapon.

That last one isn’t merely theoretical. A “misuse” report Anthropic made public earlier this month detailed five cases in which foreign scientists tried to evade Claude’s guardrails on “gain of function” inquiries. That’s a euphemism for when scientists tinker with a pathogen’s genes to enhance it in some way, making it more infectious, deadlier, or better able to spread among mammals, for example.

highlights.title: Gavin Newsom signs laws to protect California workers from AI threat
highlights.summary: Democratic governor sharply critical of Donald Trump for not passing comprehensive federal AI regulations. Governor Gavin Newsom signed laws Wednesday aimed at protecting California workers from the threats of artificial intelligence, including potential job losses and workplace surveillance.
body: The laws ban employers from using the technology to predict a worker’s emotional state by using their biometric data, require employers to send written notices to workers if AI is responsible for mass layoffs and ban employers from relying on AI to decide to fire someone.

The Democratic governor also signed an executive order to require state agencies to continue to refer to the technology as “artificial intelligence” instead of the term “super intelligence” as Donald Trump recently ordered US diplomats to use.
“AI should expand opportunity – not come at the expense of workers and families,” Newsom said in a statement. “As this technology reshapes the workplace, California is putting people at the center.”

highlights.title: The AI Tamagotchis are coming
highlights.summary: While AI has made plenty of inroads on people's phones and computers, it's largely failed in dedicated devices. But over the next year, two major AI companies, Meta and OpenAI, will attempt to change that.
body: Personal AI hardware has mostly crashed and burned. OpenAI and Meta are counting on two selling points: It’s useful, and it’s cute.

“Hardware is hard” is a tech industry mantra. Dedicated AI devices like the Friend and Humane AI Pin have inspired mainly frustration and backlash, which may only worsen as public anger toward AI grows. Meta and OpenAI, however, are both pushing ahead. OpenAI is working with famed ex-Apple designer Jony Ive and plans to ship no earlier than February 2027, per a public filing. Meta aims to launch a pendant-like device sooner, before this year’s holiday shopping season.

While OpenAI’s hardware didn’t make an appearance at this year’s DevDay, the company debuted a major new AI agent platform called Dots, complete with personalizable colored blobs with eyes. During a Q&A with reporters after the keynote, when asked whether Dots would make their way into a future physical hardware device, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman replied that that “seems like a very reasonable thing to assume we may do someday,” declining to offer further details.

highlights.title: White Sox sweep aside Astros to end 21-year wait for playoff series win
highlights.summary: Meidroth’s three-run homer powers Chicago to 7-3 win. White Sox win first playoff series since 2005 title. Chicago advance to face Cleveland in AL Division Series. The Chicago White Sox used a big first inning and a three-run homer from Chase Meidroth to propel them to a 7-3 win over the Houston…
body: It’s the first time Chicago has won a playoff series since beating Houston in the World Series in 2005. Under the direction of second-year skipper Will Venable and with a letter of support from Pope Leo XIV, the White Sox advanced to face AL Central champion Cleveland in the AL Division Series beginning Saturday in Cleveland.
The White Sox, who lost 100 games in each of the last three seasons, are the only team in major league history to follow consecutive 100-loss seasons with a playoff berth.

The AL West-winning Astros went 81-81 to become the first team to reach the postseason without a winning record. Their recent playoff woes in Houston continued Wednesday as they dropped their ninth straight home playoff game in a ninth trip to the postseason in the last 10 years.

Chicago pounced on the Astros for four runs in the first inning, a day after scoring three in the first two innings of a 6-3 win. Houston ace Hunter Brown was lifted after getting just two outs and wasn’t helped by a sloppy defense that committed two first-inning errors.

highlights.summary: Rantzen, who fronted the BBC's That's Life for two decades, went on to found Childline, and in recent years had been a campaigner for assisted dying.
body: Dame Esther Rantzen, who presented BBC show That's Life! for 21 years and launched the charity Childline, has died at the age of 86.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the veteran broadcaster and campaigner had "changed countless lives".
Dame Esther hosted and produced That's Life! during its run from 1973 to 1994. It regularly attracted 20 million viewers for its mixture of serious consumer investigations and light-hearted items.

She launched Childline, a British counselling service for children and young people, in 1986, and in 2013 she launched Silver Line to help elderly people suffering from isolation and loneliness. Later in life, she became a prominent campaigner for the legalisation of assisted dying.

highlights.title: Stella McCartney makes waves with ‘sea life, not sea food’ theme in zero-wool Paris show
highlights.summary: Designer showcases wool alternatives and ocean-inspired clothes and says ‘kindness requires real work’ Stella McCartney has been talking about animal rights at fashion week for 30 years. She is usually a lone voice, but the issue is back in the headlines this season.
body: “There is no wool on the runway this season, and I’m proud of that,” McCartney said after her show. She has been working on wool alternatives, including Brewed Protein, a fermented alternative to cashmere and wool developed in collaboration with the Japanese biotech firm Spiber, which was first used in her collections a year ago.

The issue, she says, is “a tricky one. I’ve got alpacas at home, and I have to shear them. If you can shear a sheep in a kind, humane way, then I don’t, personally, think that’s the end of the world. When we do have wool in our collections it is responsibly sourced. But the way a lot of [wool production] is done today is deeply cruel.

“At the end of the day it’s about how kind you are, but monitoring that kindness requires real work. At Stella, we police everything from start to finish at my cost, at my time. If I use wool, I can show you exactly where it’s coming from, and I’m proud of that. But I’m alone in that, and I shouldn’t be.”

body: Google.org announced on Sept. 15 that the MIT Transit Lab is a recipient of $2.1 million in funding — one of only 15 projects selected in the worldwide Google.org Impact Challenge: AI for Government Innovation. The funding from Google’s philanthropic arm will support NGOs, social enterprises, and academic institutions as they integrate artificial intelligence-powered solutions across topics like health, resilience, and economy.

The Transit Lab’s winning project, the Public Transit Intelligence Hub (PTIQ), aims to unify public transportation agencies’ real-time monitoring, operations control, and passenger communication systems into a single centralized AI-orchestrated platform that will allow transit control center staff to make better-informed, on-the-spot decisions, and provide riders with more immediate and accurate information.
